deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page and the next one (exact ray trace with r = 1794.249, log n = 0.1838592 → n ≈ 1.5271, log n = 0.2150906 → n ≈ 1.6409) show a two-lens achromatic objective of crown and flint glass. The paraxial optics is handled with Gauss's recursive scheme, the one later published in the Dioptrische Untersuchungen of 1840/41. The quantities are, with logarithms written in the 10-offset convention:
- f, f', f'', f''' are the reduced surface powers. log f = 6.4679863 gives f = 2.93756e-4; f' = 7.37685e-4; f'' = -8.7975e-4 (the 'n' marks a negative number); f''' = 2.61016e-4.
- h, h', h'' are the reduced thicknesses or separations. log h = 0.9591556 gives h = 9.102394; h' = 0 (the lenses are in contact); log h'' = 0.8183332 gives h'' ≈ 6.5816.

Previous page. The first fundamental solution starts with α = 1, β = f and follows the recursion
  α_{k+1} = -α_k + β_k h_k,
  β_{k+1} = -β_k + α_{k+1} f_{k+1}.
It ends at α''' = -0.99632527, β''' = -0.00041212 and α'''/β''' = 2417.538. This is a parallel incoming ray, so 2417.538 is the back focal distance.

This page. The second fundamental solution starts with γ = 0, δ = 1 and uses the same recursion.
- γ' = -γ + δ h = +9.102394.
- δ' = -δ + γ' f'. The log of γ' f' is 0.9591556 + 6.8678701, so γ' f' = 0.006714686 and δ' = -0.993285314.
- γ'' = -γ' + δ' h' = -9.102394, since h' = 0.
- δ'' = -δ' + γ'' f''. Here γ'' f'' = (+)0.008007843 (both logs carry n), so δ'' = +1.001293157.
- γ''' = -γ'' + δ'' h''. The log of δ'' is 0.0005613 and the log of h'' is 0.8183332, so δ'' h'' = 6.590138 and γ''' = 9.102394 + 6.590138 = 15.692532.
- δ''' = -δ'' + γ''' f'''. The log of γ''' is 1.1956930, so γ''' f''' = 0.004095997 and δ''' = -0.997197163.

Next Gauss computes x = (1+δ''')/β'''. The numerator 1+δ''' = 0.00280284 has log 7.4475978. The denominator β''' has log 6.6150277n. The difference is log 0.8325701n, giving x = -6.800958.
- [mine] x is the position of one cardinal point, most likely the first principal point, measured from the first vertex in the computation's length unit.
- [mine] The scheme has unit determinant: α'''δ''' - β'''γ''' = 1, to 7 places.

Marginal unit conversion. The focal distance 2417.533 units is set equal to 510 Bavarian lines (the margin note '510 L. Bayr.'). The side column reads:
- log 6.800958 = 0.83257
- log 510 = 2.70757
- their sum is 3.54014
- log 2417.533 = 3.38337
- [mine] difference 0.15677, which is the log of 1.4347.
Hence the note '1^L 4347 Bayr', i.e. x = 1.4347 Bavarian lines. This is converted to 1.2912 Paris lines, and the note '2^mm 9' gives about 2.9 mm (1.4347 × 2.0268 mm ≈ 2.908 mm).

Bottom of the page. The numbers 1.7529070, 1.9074220 and 3.2538828 appear. The last is log r = log 1794.249, the radius used on the next page. The purpose of the other two logarithms (≈ log 56.60 and log 80.82) is not determinable from this page.
errors: No arithmetic errors found in the γ/δ recursion; all logarithms and sums check to the last place given.

Paris-line conversion is slightly off: 1.4347 Bavarian lines (2.0268 mm each) ≈ 2.908 mm ≈ 1.289 Paris lines (2.2558 mm), not 1.2912. Gauss's ratio 1.4347/1.2912 ≈ 1.1111 suggests a rounded conversion factor (about 10/9) rather than 1.1130.
The focal value 2417.533 used in the margin differs trivially from 2417.538 on the previous page (rounding or a slip in the last digit).

results.what: Second fundamental solution (γ=0, δ=1) of the paraxial recursion for a lens system through alternating reduced powers and thicknesses; together with the α/β solution it gives the full paraxial transfer, with unit determinant
results.modern_name: Gaussian brackets / paraxial ray-transfer (ABCD) matrix of a thick-lens system

results.what: Location of a principal point of the objective, x = (1+δ''')/β''' = -6.800958 units ≈ 1.43 Bavarian lines ≈ 2.9 mm
results.modern_name: principal-plane (Hauptpunkt) position of a thick lens system

deep.surprise_reason: This is a numerical application of Gauss's own published dioptric scheme (cardinal points via recursive brackets) to a concrete achromatic objective. It is valuable working material showing his method in use, but contains nothing beyond what he published in 1841.

checkable.asserts: x converted to Bavarian lines with focal length = 510 lines

transcription_corrections: The formula for x reads x = (1+δ''')/β''' (denominator β''', whose log 6.6150277n is written beside it), not γ'''.
δ' should read -0.99328 5314 (stray point in the transcription '-0.9932.85314').
'Phys. 1' is a pencil archival mark; '(21)' is the circled folio number; '22' (with a struck-out number) is an older foliation.
The '-6.4' at left margin belongs to the facing page (bleed of '-6,4' from the previous page), not to this computation.
The faint pencil '4433' before '2^mm 9' is uncertain; '2^mm 9' means 2.9 mm, the metric value of x.
The side column 0,83257 / 2.70757 / 3.54014 / 3.38337 is a log computation: log x + log 510 - log 2417.533 = log 1.4347.
